text.title: What Should This Gate Do When It Cannot Evaluate
text.summary: Routing from an observable property of the gate's code to the fix. The first two branches cover most gates in most repositories.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the gate have a terminating path that reports pass without having produced a verdict — an empty default from an exception handler, an unchecked exit status, or a checker nobody invokes?

conclusion.verdict: Gate is fail-closed. Record the contract with `last_proved` set to today and move on. Re-run the fault-injection proof whenever the gate, its parser, or its provider changes.
Unproven, not closed. Break one check on purpose and confirm a non-zero exit before claiming coverage. An assertion of fail-closed that has never been observed failing is a claim, not a gate.

Replace the default return with a synthetic finding at the gate's own blocking severity, carrying the mode, the case id and the first 200 chars of the raw response. Do NOT raise — raising changes every caller and the patch will not merge. Then enumerate the remaining four modes (r2).
Accumulate each sub-check's status (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` when piping) and exit on the accumulator. Verify by breaking one sub-check; the runner must exit non-zero.
Either wire the invocation into a runner and record it in the contract, or delete the config file. A config with no invocation is a coverage claim nobody can falsify — the worst of the three states.

Structured output closes PARSE only. Explicitly handle REFUSAL, TRUNCATION (stop_reason == length), TRANSPORT and EMPTY — a schema-valid response carrying no verdict is the mode that survives the schema fix.

A human gate fails closed by default — an unreviewed artefact is simply not approved. Record it as `instrument: manual` with modes `absent_input` and `crash`, state the cost in founder-hours, and do not call it deterministic. Its real risk is not fail-open; it is that the same defect is re-found every session, which is a placement problem (see `verification-rung-placement-rule`).
Add one named, logged, expiring `--allow-degraded` flag rather than letting someone remove the gate. No expiry date means you have shipped a hole with a nicer name.
